chunks: From him, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAbd Ṣāliḥ عليه السلام, who said:

A man may give the adhan while he is sitting, but he should not give the iqamah except while standing. And he said: You may give the adhan while riding, but do not give the iqamah except while you are on the ground.

key_terms.جَالِسٌ: sitting, a permitted state for giving the adhan
key_terms.رَاكِبٌ: riding, indicating permissibility for adhan while mounted
key_terms.عَلَى الْأَرْضِ: on the ground, meaning not mounted when giving the iqamah
key_terms.قَائِمٌ: standing, the required posture for iqamah in this report
key_terms.يُؤَذِّنُ: to pronounce the adhan, the call to prayer
key_terms.يُقِيمُ: to pronounce the iqamah, the commencement call before salat

ai.seo_question: Can the adhan be given while sitting or riding, and must the iqamah be given standing?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the adhan may be delivered while sitting or while riding, indicating flexibility in its performance. By contrast, the iqamah is restricted to a more formal posture and state: it should be given while standing and while on the ground.
